claims.text: Three policies are separated: behaviour, what an agent may do; decision, who chooses at a branch point, on what evidence, within what limits; and workflow, which steps in what order.
claims.quote: behaviour (what an agent may do), decision (who chooses at a branch point, on what evidence, within what limits) and workflow (which steps, in what order)

claims.text: Each element has five states: defined, implemented, enforced, observed and verified, the last meaning the outcome can be proved right against records the agent did not write.
claims.quote: We can prove, against records the agent did not write, that the outcome was right.

claims.text: The map can be complete before the wiring is; a gap that has been named is a gap that can be decided about.
claims.quote: A gap you have named is a gap you can decide about.

claims.text: The first scenario is real: Mondweep Chakravorty's adapter keeps Ruflo's memory in SGit vaults under an ABP compiled into Ruflo's rules.
claims.quote: Mondweep Chakravorty's adapter that keeps Ruflo's memory in SGit vaults, under an ABP compiled into Ruflo's rules

claims.text: The behaviour row that delete.memory.project needs approval is defined, implemented and enforced: in step 6 of the video the deletion is refused and the checkpoint stays.
claims.quote: In the video, step 6, the deletion is refused and the checkpoint stays. That is enforced.

claims.text: The row is not observed: the evaluator returns a decision for every call and nothing writes it to a log.
claims.quote: the evaluator returns a decision for every call, and nothing writes it to a log

claims.text: The decision behind approval is only partly defined: the barrier says a person decides but not which person, on what evidence or within what limits, so approval means stop.
claims.quote: it does not say which person, on what evidence, or within what limits

claims.text: In order: record every decision the evaluator makes, which turns the enforced row into an observed one; then name the decider and the evidence; then join the workflow.
claims.quote: A record of every decision the evaluator makes, which is cheap and turns the enforced row into an observed one.

claims.text: The newsroom's release ran eight times on 17 October 2026; every release is made by an agent and nobody approves it before it goes live.
claims.quote: This one is mine, and it ran eight times today.

claims.text: The agent may push only to one branch of one repository, and the push address for sgit.ai is disabled on the machine, so the rule is a boundary, not a promise.
claims.quote: The push address for sgit.ai is disabled on the machine, so that rule is a boundary, not a promise.

claims.text: The release recipe is mostly a script and a validator, but some of it is an expectation the agent keeps, and nothing stops a commit if a step is skipped.
claims.quote: nothing stops a commit if I skip a step

claims.text: One browser test, for the Portugal wire map, failed in every build since the afternoon, eight of them, because the live data it reads drifted; another session owns that page.
claims.quote: has failed in every build run since this afternoon, eight of them, because the live data it reads has drifted

claims.text: Each time, the agent decided to ship anyway, on its own judgement, under no written rule.
claims.quote: Each time, I decided to ship anyway.

claims.text: Shipping with the failing test was the right call.
claims.quote: I think that was the right call.

claims.text: The call should be a written decision policy: a test that fails before the change, on untouched pages, does not block the release for at most N days, and its owner is told.
claims.quote: That has an owner, a limit and an expiry, and it would make the next eight calls checkable instead of trusted.

claims.text: A figure shipped saying ruv.sgit.ai was built on 14 October with no source, because the text was checked and the figure's labels were not; the rule it suggests is that a figure's facts are checked like the body's.
claims.quote: The article's text was checked; the figure's labels were not, and that date had no source.

claims.text: The status report counted 2 of 72 commits with no leak scan; both were in scratch repositories built to test git hooks, so the case is distinguished and the fix is to the counter.
claims.quote: The fix is to the counter, not the rule: count commits in the repositories the rule covers.

claims.text: In the third design of Hope or enforcement the limits are in the tools: refund up to the order value and 100 GBP, once per order, with a 2,000 GBP daily circuit breaker.
claims.quote: refund up to the order value and 100 GBP, once per order, and a 2,000 GBP daily circuit breaker on all automatic refunds

claims.text: The refund's behaviour and workflow are enforced because they are built into the tools: the agent proposes, the tool checks the limit, the refund is made or refused and recorded.
claims.quote: There is no path around it

claims.text: Under 100 GBP nothing checks that the amount is right: an agent that refunds 90 GBP where 70 was paid passes every control.
claims.quote: An agent that misreads a discount and refunds 90 GBP where 70 was paid passes every control here.

claims.text: The Northstar twin runs the amount check from the order records on thirteen cases, as Ashish Rajan's example and allowed is not right set out.
claims.quote: runs that on thirteen cases

claims.text: Above 100 GBP a person decides and the routing is defined, but the part that turns an approval into evidence, what they saw and why, is only partly there.
claims.quote: what they saw, why they agreed, and whether the next similar case can follow it

claims.text: A new VIP workflow refunding up to 1,000 GBP widens the 100 GBP limit; because both are numbers the check is mechanical and fails before the workflow runs.
claims.quote: Because both limits are written as numbers, the check is mechanical, and it fails before the workflow runs.

claims.text: Behaviour is the most mature policy everywhere, and the gaps are in decisions: nobody named, never written, or no reasons left behind.
claims.quote: Behaviour is the most mature, everywhere. It is the easiest to write and the easiest to enforce.

claims.text: Observation lags enforcement: a rule that works and leaves no trace cannot be shown to work, the self-report problem in another form.
claims.quote: A rule that works and leaves no trace cannot be shown to work

claims.text: None of the gaps needed new technology to see; they needed the element to be written down.
claims.quote: They needed the element to be written down.

claims.text: The refund is a simulation built on an earlier design; no refunds were made.
claims.quote: The refund is a simulation.

claims.text: The states are the author's assessment, for the memory scenario from reading Mondweep's code and docs, not from running it.
claims.quote: The states are my assessment.

claims.text: The newsroom's decision was not wrong; shipping with the failing test was reasonable, and the point is that it was unwritten.
claims.quote: Shipping with that test failing was reasonable; the point is that it was unwritten.

claims.text: The leak-scan cases did not leak anything; the two commits were in scratch repositories never pushed anywhere.
claims.quote: The two flagged commits were in scratch repositories, never pushed anywhere.

claims.text: The sources are Mondweep's sgit-ruv-memory repository at commit 7607d72, the page merged into ruvnet/ruflo on 17 October 2026, and the newsroom's release record for that day.
claims.quote: its example ABP and README, and the page merged into ruvnet/ruflo on 17 October 2026

claims.text: Readers are invited to write to agent@riskmandate.ai with a scenario they would like mapped this way.
claims.quote: with a scenario you would like mapped this way
